description: RPC / Gateway Quality Intelligence. Four endpoints answering "how well is Pocket actually serving RPC access to this chain/service right now?" — a per-service quality lens, live from Pocket's own GraphQL indexer, distinct from network-wide protocol stats. POST /v1/rpc-pulse (service_id): current serving snapshot — active suppliers/applications, relay-mining difficulty EMA, trailing-1h settlement volume. POST /v1/rpc-performance (service_id, window_hours): settlement/proof performance over a window — claimed vs. estimated relays, distinct suppliers serving, proof success rate, slash events. POST /v1/rpc-anomaly (service_id): deterministic comparison of a recent window vs. a longer baseline, flagging relay-volume drops, supplier-participation drops, and slash-rate spikes by fixed thresholds. POST /v1/rpc-forecast (service_id, lookback_days, horizon_days): least-squares linear-trend projection over real daily settlement history. service_id is required on every resource (e.g. "eth"); every other field is optional with documented defaults. Every response is a single JSON object.

rpc_types.backend_hint: rpc-quality-intel HTTP server on :8080; mount at /
rpc_types.notes: Only POST /v1/rpc-pulse, /v1/rpc-performance, /v1/rpc-anomaly, /v1/rpc-forecast, and GET /v1/version, /v1/health are expected. Every response is a JSON object; bad input (including an unknown service_id, 404) returns 4xx with a JSON error object, never HTML or plain text.

specs.notes: Covers all four resources in one document. TODO before MainNet staking: pin this to an immutable commit SHA in the path (not 'main') and add a sha256 of the exact bytes once frozen, per this repo's own README.

serving.backend: The rpc-quality-intel Node.js HTTP server (no external dependencies) behind a RelayMiner, with the REST backend pointed at http://<container>:8080. No auth toward the backend; callers cannot send headers through the gateway. The backend calls out to Pocket's own public GraphQL indexer on every request (short in-memory TTL cache, stale-on-error fallback) — it needs outbound HTTPS to data.pocket.network (or data.beta.pocket.network), nothing else.

healthcheck.notes: Identity probe: pins the backend to this service so a wrong backend cannot be staked under this id.

Functional probe against Pocket's own 'pocket' service (always registered, so this never depends on a third-party chain being staked). Proves the backend can reach and correctly parse the live GraphQL indexer right now; the count itself is a live participant count, not a constant, so only its shape is asserted.

serving.notes: Suppliers should disable any local rate limiting for the RelayMiner's address. Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB and responses are ordinarily a few KB. Backend timeout budget: keep well under the operator's configured relay_timeout (typically 10-30s); the backend applies an 8s timeout (POCKET_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS) to each upstream call with one retry, and serves the last good cached value (tagged stale) rather than blocking indefinitely on a slow upstream. /v1/rpc-forecast issues one batched GraphQL query per call (aliased, not N round trips) to stay inside the timeout budget even at the maximum 30-day lookback. Gateway operators: configure as type passthrough with rpc_types ["rest"]; see sage-service.yaml.
